question: In a PLHIV presenting with respiratory distress, a resting SpO₂ of 92% on air is sufficient to exclude severe PCP without the need for arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. SpO₂ ≥ 94% alone is inadequate in high-suspicion PCP. ABG is required to calculate the alveolar-arterial (A-a) gradient, which identifies severe PCP (PaO₂ < 70 mmHg) warranting corticosteroids alongside co-trimoxazole.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. An SpO₂ of 92% does not exclude severe PCP; ABG is mandatory when SpO₂ ≤ 94% or when clinical suspicion is high. PaO₂ < 70 mmHg or A-a gradient ≥ 35 mmHg defines severe PCP and is the threshold for adding adjuvant corticosteroids.
